tools.name: gate_list_apps
tools.description: Read the project's apps, allowed calls, limits, state, idle flags and anomaly-guard settings. Use it to select an app id. Create or revoke apps on the setup endpoint, /mcp/setup.

tools.name: gate_list_approvers
tools.description: Approvers are people who decide held actions. List active and revoked dedicated approvers with ids, names and creation times; never returns keys or hashes. Team members with the approver role are a separate list. Requires the project owner key or an active member key. Create or revoke dedicated keys

tools.name: gate_create_run
tools.description: Gate Actions: give one agent session narrow, expiring permission. Actions are rules with {placeholders} bound by scope (e.g. "PATCH /customers/{customer}/tickets/:id" with scope {"customer":"A"}), each with an optional max and approval. Check gate_list_approvers for an active human approver before g

tools.name: gate_delegate_run
tools.description: Hand a narrower run to another active app in the same project. Uses the parent app key and run token, never the admin key. Scope, expiry, approvals and ancestor budgets stay enforced; maximum depth five.

tools.name: gate_revoke_run
tools.description: End one run granted with gate_create_run: its token stops working at once (403 run_revoked) while the app itself keeps working. Use it to stop an agent mid-job; grant a new run with gate_create_run if the work should continue.

tools.name: gate_list_actions
tools.description: Which actions are waiting for a human decision? Read held actions (pending by default, or another requested state) and their exact calls; this tool cannot decide or resubmit them. Approving or rejecting a held action is done by a person with an approver key in the dashboard, by design. No MCP tool c

tools.name: gate_read_audit
tools.description: Which gateway calls happened recently? Returns recent gateway calls (time, app, matched route, status, reason, duration); use it to investigate individual calls across the project rather than gate_get_metrics aggregates or a single gate_get_run_timeline. Newest first, with totals by status and refus

tools.name: gate_export_audit_proof
tools.description: Which signed audit records can I export for verification? Returns chained audit rows, decided-action feature snapshots and signed anchors; use it for a portable tamper-evident export instead of gate_read_audit's recent-call view, then check it with gate_verify_audit_proof. No sealed paths/bodies, no

tools.name: gate_verify_audit_proof
tools.description: Is this signed audit export intact? Returns intact or broken_at for a supplied signed export; use it to check a gate_export_audit_proof export rather than retrieve audit rows. Recomputes the chain and project signature; broken_at is a one-based row position. Does not approve actions or change permis

tools.name: gate_get_metrics
tools.description: What are the project call trends and current usage? Returns project-wide 24-hour call aggregates, anomaly scores, idle apps and current-month usage; use it for operational trends rather than individual calls in gate_read_audit or one run in gate_get_run_timeline. Includes stored call counts by HTTP

tools.name: gate_get_run_timeline
tools.description: What happened during this run? Returns one run's call metadata, approvals and approver names, recovery outcomes and delegated children; use it to reconstruct that session instead of gate_read_audit's project-wide calls or gate_get_run_tree's permission state. No bodies or query values. One run only;

tools.name: gate_get_run_tree
tools.description: Which permissions and delegated descendants does this run have? Returns one run and its delegated descendants without tokens; use it to inspect delegation and permission state instead of gate_get_run_timeline events. One run only; the project-wide log is gate_read_audit.

tools.name: gate_explain_refusal
tools.description: What a Gate refusal means and how to fix it, from the x-gate-refused header value (e.g. route_not_allowed).

tools.name: gate_learn_suggestions
tools.description: Read normalized routes and a suggested per-minute limit from an admin-enabled, time-boxed learning session. Records only method, normalized path templates and counts per minute; no query values, raw ids, headers or bodies. Never enables learning or applies rules.

tools.name: gate_update_app
tools.description: Apply stored learning suggestions to an existing app and return the applied routes, suggested per-minute limit and learning-session metadata. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "oversight" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: gate_create_run, gate_get_metrics · Private data: gate_create_run, gate_delegate_run, gate_revoke_run, gate_export_audit_proof, gate_get_run_tree, gate_learn_suggestions · Public sink: gate_create_run, gate_get_metrics · Destructive: gate_create_run, gate_delegate_run, gate_revoke_run, gate_read_audit, gate_get_metrics, gate_get_run_timeline, gate_get_run_tree.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: gate_create_run, gate_get_metrics · Private data: gate_create_run, gate_delegate_run, gate_revoke_run, gate_export_audit_proof, gate_get_run_tree, gate_learn_suggestions · Public sink: gate_create_run, gate_get_metrics · Destructive: gate_create_run, gate_delegate_run, gate_revoke_run, gate_read_audit, gate_get_metrics, gate_get_run_timeline, gate_get_run_tree

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
